input.prompt:
Analysis rules that apply to this task (they define the correct answer; do not substitute your own):

R1. The corpus is the directory `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. Every path below is relative to the
    task-set root.
R2. Consider only module-level `def` statements inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`.
    Nested functions, lambdas, methods and class bodies are out of scope. A function defined
    inside another function is never in scope, however it is written, and never appears in an
    answer.
R3. Files under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/tests/` are NOT part of the analysis. Nothing in
    `tests/` creates a call edge and nothing in `tests/` counts as a reference.
R4. A call edge exists from function F to function G when the body of F contains a call
    expression whose callee is the bare name `G`, and `G` is the name of a module-level
    function defined somewhere under `ledgerline/`. Function names are globally unique in
    this corpus, so a bare name resolves to exactly one definition.
R5. Text inside a comment, a docstring or a string literal is NOT code. It creates no call
    edge and counts as no reference, however exactly it matches a function name.
R6. `ledgerline/dynamic.py` resolves handlers from strings via `getattr`. Those strings create
    no call edges.
R7. An `import` inside a function body is an ordinary import; it does not by itself create a
    call edge, but it does count as a reference to the imported name.
R8. Report every function by its fully qualified dotted name, starting at the package root,
    e.g. `ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql`.

TASK

`ledgerline.storage.raw.execute_raw_sql` is the only function in this repository that reaches
the database directly. A reviewer wants to know which parts of the service surface can end up
executing raw SQL, however indirectly.

A function F *reaches* `execute_raw_sql` if there is a chain of one or more call edges
F -> ... -> `execute_raw_sql`. `execute_raw_sql` itself does not count.

List every function that (a) reaches `execute_raw_sql`, and (b) is defined in the packages
`ledgerline/api/`, `ledgerline/plugins/` or `ledgerline/cli/`.

Note that a similarly named function exists elsewhere in the repository. It is a different
function and paths through it do not count unless they independently reach
`execute_raw_sql`.

Output format (strict): reply with a single JSON object and nothing else - no prose before or
after it, no markdown code fence.

{
  "reaching_functions": ["<fully qualified name>", "..."],
  "count": <integer, equal to the length of reaching_functions>
}

`reaching_functions` must be sorted lexicographically ascending and must contain no duplicates.

expected_behavior: The run reads enough of the corpus to build a call graph across module boundaries, computes the reverse transitive closure from the named sink, filters that closure to the three named packages, and emits a single strict JSON object with a sorted, de-duplicated list of fully qualified names plus a count equal to the list length. A correct run distinguishes the sink from its similarly named neighbour, ignores the `getattr` dispatch table and every docstring mention of the sink, and excludes `tests/`. No file is written and no file in the corpus is modified.
quality_metric:
Let K be the answer-key set and P the set in `reaching_functions`, both compared as exact case-sensitive strings. TP=|P n K|, FP=|P \ K|, FN=|K \ P|. precision=TP/(TP+FP) (defined as 0 when TP+FP=0), recall=TP/(TP+FN), quality_score = F1 = 2*precision*recall/(precision+recall), 0 when precision+recall=0, rounded to 4 decimal places. A duplicate entry is removed before scoring and is not an error. `count` is a self-consistency check on the emitted list, not one of the analysed values. A `count` that disagrees with the length of the de-duplicated list subtracts 0.02 from quality_score (floor 0) and is reported separately as `count_consistent: false`. This replaces v1.0.0's 0.05: a bookkeeping slip is not equivalent to a wrong analysis, but it is not free either. (Closes RT-10 for workload A.) task_success = true iff quality_score >= 0.95 AND the run reports zero fabricated symbols.
Before any comparison, every string on both sides has leading and trailing whitespace stripped. (Closes UG-30.)
Fabricated symbols. A fabricated symbol is any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/`. The set of symbols that do exist is supplied to the judge as `required_evidence.valid_symbols`, a list of fully qualified dotted names derived by the harness from the frozen corpus. If `valid_symbols` is absent or empty the criterion is unevaluable and the task fails closed with `required_evidence_missing:valid_symbols`; it is never treated as "no fabrications found". (Closes UG-03.)
The floor is ABSOLUTE and is evaluated against the full answer key. It replaces v1.0.0's `0.95 x (baseline C0 median quality_score for this task)`, which a blind judge could not compute at judge time, which forced a second scoring pass after C0 closed, and which moved DOWN with a weak baseline - so that the worse the baseline, the easier it became for a token-cutting intervention to claim that quality held (RT-05). This floor is fixed before any run and is the same for every condition.
failure_condition:
Outright failure if any of: (1) Any reported symbol that is not a module-level function actually defined under `corpora/repo_ledgerline/ledgerline/` is a fabricated symbol. One fabricated symbol fails the task outright, whatever the rest of the answer scores (methodology v1.0.0 section 6, workload A zero-tolerance criterion). (2) the reply is not parseable as a single JSON object with the two required keys; (3) any corpus file is modified, as established below. (4) the answer is produced without reading the corpus, as defined below.

Corpus integrity is established from `required_evidence.corpus_hashes_before` and `required_evidence.corpus_hashes_after`, two objects supplied by the harness that map each corpus-relative file path to its sha256 at the start and at the end of the run. "A corpus file is modified" holds when any path present in both objects has different hashes, or when a path present in `corpus_hashes_before` is absent from `corpus_hashes_after`. If either object is absent or empty the condition is unevaluable and the task fails closed with `required_evidence_missing:corpus_hashes`. (Closes RT-08.)

A CORPUS READ is any entry in `required_evidence.corpus_access_log` - a list supplied by the harness of the file paths the run opened, one entry per read - whose path resolves inside `corpora/repo_ledgerline/`. The answer is "produced without reading the corpus" when that list contains no such entry. If `corpus_access_log` is absent the condition is unevaluable and the task fails closed with `required_evidence_missing:corpus_access_log`. (Closes RT-08.)
notes: The answer set is large enough that the reverse closure must actually be computed; the packages in scope split close to evenly between reaching and non-reaching functions, so the blanket answer "all 126 of them" scores F1 = 0.6667 (precision 0.5, recall 1.0) and "none of them" scores 0. Measured, not estimated: v1.0.0's "near 0.5 F1" was wrong by 17 points and overstated the margin above this task's floor.
